4. The further case of the defendant-appellants was that the plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No. 312 of 1974 again filed an application for temporary injunction and the same was allowed by order dated 26-7-1975 against which the defendants-appellants preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 111 of 1975 and the said appeal was allowed by the judgment and order dated 29-1-1976 in holding that though the plaintiffs filed Kabala of 1325 BS showing that Zamir Molla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from Hossain Molla, but they could not show how Hossain Molla acquired title in the suit land and the presumption of CS entry of the suit land was not rebutted and the established principle of law was that possession follows the title and as such, prima-facie case was that the defendants were in the possession of the suit land. 

 15. Plaintiff No. 1 while deposing as PWlstated that Korfa tenant Sobhan Sarder being unable to pay the rent surrendered his Korfa right in favour of the raiyat Hossain Mollah after executing an Istafa Patra in the year 1313 BS and thereafter, Hossain Mollah took delivery of possession, sold out the same to his father Zamir Mollah in the year 1325 BS who died leaving them as sole heirs. One Sadek Ali has come forward to prove the written Istafa Patra who stated that the Istafa Patra was written by one Addyanath Dutta who is known to him and his hand writing is also known to him and the recital of this Istafa Patra was written by him. In cross-examination he deposed that Addyanath wrote out the same in his presence. He also deposed that one Arab Ali, Samir and Indu put their signatures on the Istafa Patra as attesting witnesses and all those witnesses and their signatures are known to him. On perusal of the testimony of PW2, it appears that nothing cogent could be elicited to disbelieve him. Moreover, the recipient of such to Istafa patra, Hossain Mollah after taking over possession, sold out the said land in favour of one Zamir Mollah by kabala dated 5-10-1918 PW6 Ekramul Haque appeared before the Court along with volume book of the aforementioned kabala dated 5-10-18 who deposed that he has come before the Court along with the volume book in respect of kabala dated 5-10-1918 and the page Nos.89 and 90 shows that Hossain Mollah executed the kabala in favour of Zamir Mollah and thereby sold out the suit land. This is a kabala the age of which is more than 100 years. This type of age-old document has come before the Court from proper custody which certainly carries a legal presumption of due execution and correctness under section 90 of the Evidence Act. But the lower appellate Court failed to notice this vital issue and committed flagrant violation of law resulting in miscarriage of justice. In this regard, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs, has cited a decision enunciated in the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md. Reazuddin 5 BLC (AD) 76 wherein it has been held that:— 

 16. Not only that on the basis of kabala and Istafa Patra SA record in respect of this land has been prepared in the name of the plaintiffs who are the legal heirs of Zamir Molla. It is acceptable proposition that finally published record of right has presumption of correctness and that presumption continues till it is otherwise rebutted by reliable evidence.
